title: About AI Resources - AI Software Libraries

blocks.text: AI Software Libraries are the third-party and internal packages that power AI development and runtime, such as frameworks for model training and inference, SDKs for calling LLMs, orchestration or agent frameworks, vector database clients, and supporting utilities. These libraries are a critical part of the AI supply chain as they can introduce vulnerabilities, unsafe capabilities, and license or compliance obligations into AI applications and agent workflows.

Zscaler's AI Security enables tracking of AI software libraries, thereby helping security and platform teams understand what components AI systems rely on, assess exposure, e.g., risky dependencies or outdated versions), and enforce organizational policies for secure and compliant AI deployments.
The AI Resources - AI Software Libraries page provides a tabular view of AI resources that exist across all the onboarded cloud accounts:
The AI Resources - AI Software Libraries page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: See which AI libraries are being used across projects and where they’re deployed.
Spot restrictive licenses, e.g., GPL and AGPL early to avoid distribution or commercial-use issues.
Identify high-risk or vulnerable dependencies so you can prioritize upgrades or replacements.
Pinpoint the library that may be driving a security, policy, or build issue.
Align teams on approved libraries and versions to reduce drift and surprise changes.
Produce evidence of license and dependency posture without manual tracking.
Allows organizations to monitor and evaluate supply chain vulnerabilities associated with their AI-related assets.

blocks.heading: About AI Resources - AI Software Libraries Page

blocks.text: On the AI Resources - AI Software Libraries Page, (AI Infrastructure > AI Resources > AI Software Libraries), you can do the following

blocks.item: Filter by Business Units.
View the following widgets for a quick, at-a-glance summary of your AI software library inventory:

AI Software Libraries by Risk Level: Distribution of software libraries by their severity across known vulnerabilities (CVEs) and supply chain signals, e.g., Critical, High, Medium, Low, or None (no known vulnerabilities and a clean supply chain profile).

AI Software Libraries by Status: Distribution of the software libraries by their governance status, e.g., Sanctioned (reviewed and approved), Unsanctioned (reviewed and not approved), or Unreviewed (awaiting review).
AI Software Libraries by License Type: Distribution of AI software libraries by their license types, i.e., the license declared for each library. The license types are as follows:
Permissive Licenses: Have fewer redistribution requirements, e.g., AGPL-3.0, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, and MIT.
Copyleft Licenses: Require derivative works to be open-sourced and may increase compliance risk in commercial deployments, e.g., GPL and AGPL.
Search for a specific AI Software Library.
Apply filters to view specific data.
View a list of AI software libraries which were discovered. For each AI library, you can view:
Name & Version: The name and version of the AI library. Click the library name to view additional details.
General information: Information such as package URL, license type, language, package version, and sensitive data.
Lifecycle: Timeline of key milestones from discovery through first scans.
Graph View

The graphs consist of interactive nodes that provide contextual information (e.g., package URL, package type, license type, language, package version, supply chain risk score, and other information like package repository URL, vulnerabilities (CVEs), etc.) about the primary resource and the associated secondary resources.
The graphs also include attack paths that show how the resource is compromised, etc. This information helps you analyze the issues in detail and remediate them immediately.
Supply Chain Risk
This tab is enabled and visible only when a Supply Chain Risk Score is available for the model. If the score is not available, the tab remains hidden.
Overall Risk Score: The chart visually represents the overall risk score for the AI software library. The risk scores map to risk levels as follows
Medium: 34–55
High: 55–74
Critical: 75–100
Total Categories: The number of risk categories evaluated for this package. This score is always five and includes, Security, Dependencies, Quality, Maintenance, and Compliance.
Categories with Critical Risk: Number of categories where the category score falls in the critical range, i.e., 75–100 range.
Total Issues: Total number of failed checks across all categories. Each failed check is one issue.
Supply Risk Chain Assessment

The assessment result provides an overview of issues detected in the security techniques applied to the AI library. You can drill down each security technique to view the assigned risk score, risk level, the number of issues detected, current status of the detected issue, and remediation.
Security: Detects issues in the security testing techniques used on the AI package and assigns a risk score.
Dependencies: Detects if the dependencies are pinned to specific versions and updated automatically.
Quality: Detects issues in the code-review and branch protection practices.
Maintenance: Detects issues in the maintenance techniques.
Compliance: Detects compliance issues related to licensing and security policies.
Source: Indicates the specific location or service where the AI library was discovered, stored, or hosted.
Status: The approval status of the library. The default value is Pending Review.
Supply Chain Risk: The overall risk severity. e.g., Low, Medium, High, Critical, or Unknown.
Environment: Indicates where the asset was discovered, e.g., AWS, Azure, or GCP.
Package Type: The type of AI library, e.g., Data Manipulation & Processing, Large Language Models (LLMs), MLOps Tools, etc.
Vulnerable: Whether the library has vulnerabilities or not.
License Type: The licensing terms of the AI library, e.g., Apache-2.0.
Actions: Click the Action icon and select Sanctioned or Unsanctioned to approve or reject the package's use in the organization.
